bipartite.kami_theme: A storm wind blows down from Mount Mimuro, scattering its maple leaves into brilliant scattered color
bipartite.shimo_theme: The scattered leaves floating on the Tatsuta River are revealed to be a shimmering brocade (nishiki)
bipartite.pivot_note: The kami-no-ku describes the physical action (wind stripping the mountain of its autumn leaves) which sets up the shimo-no-ku's revelatory metaphor: the scattered leaves floating on the river's surface are perceived as if they were a woven brocade (nishiki), with なりけり marking the speaker's sudden recognition/realization of this visual truth. The whole poem is structured as a single continuous visual event moving from mountain to river, cause to perceived effect.

kigo.note: Momijiba (autumn maple leaves) is one of the most central autumn images in classical waka, epitomizing the beauty of autumn's decline; here it is the pivotal image transforming from mountain foliage into the 'brocade' floating on the river, embodying the quintessential autumn scene of maple leaves scattered by wind onto water.

source_jp:
あらし吹く

にしきなりけり
